The help action's display name in error messages is '-h/--help' (option strings joined with '/'); the value options' display names are '--a', '--b', '--c', '--d'.
- USAGE LINE (single line, no wrapping): `usage: ${prog} [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D`, terminated by one \n.
- HELP OUTPUT (exact, to stdout, then exit 0): usage line, then an empty line, then 'options:', then '  -h, --help  show this help message and exit', then '  --a A', '  --b B', '  --c C', '  --d D'; every line terminated by a single \n, no trailing blank line, no trailing spaces. Exactly two leading spaces of indent and exactly two spaces between '-h, --help' and 'show'.
- ERROR OUTPUT (exact, to stderr, then exit 2, with stdout left completely empty): write the usage line + '\n', then `${prog}: error: ${message}` + '\n'. Never wrap the message.

If a token is exactly '--', mark it as SEPARATOR and mark every remaining token to the end of the list as POSITIONAL without any further classification (no option lookup and no ambiguity check applies past the first '--'). Any 'ambiguous option' error detected in this pre-scan must be raised immediately - it outranks the help action and outranks any consume-time error, no matter where in argv it appears.
- CLASSIFY(token), applied in this exact order: (1) empty string -> POSITIONAL. (2) first char is not '-' -> POSITIONAL. (3) token is exactly one of '-h','--help','--a','--b','--c','--d' -> OPTION(action, optionString=token, explicitArg=null, sep=none). (4) token length is 1 (i.e. '-') -> POSITIONAL. (5) if the token contains '=': let head = substring before the FIRST '=', tail = the rest; if head is exactly one of the six known option strings -> OPTION(action, optionString=head, explicitArg=tail, sep='='). (6) run prefix matching (next requirement); more than one match -> raise the ambiguity error; exactly one match -> that OPTION; zero matches -> continue. (7) if the token matches /^-\d+$/ or /^-\d*\.\d+$/ -> POSITIONAL (this parser has no negative-number-looking options, so the escape always applies). (8) if the token contains a space character -> POSITIONAL. (9) otherwise -> UNKNOWN-OPTION (option-looking but no action; it goes to extras during consume).
- PREFIX MATCHING. If the token starts with '--' (chars 0 and 1 are both '-'): split off an explicit arg at the first '=' if present, giving prefix and explicitArg (null when there is no '='); then collect, in registration order (-h, --help, --a, --b, --c, --d), every option string that startsWith(prefix), each paired with that explicitArg. If the token starts with '-' but char 1 is not '-': let optionPrefix=token, shortOptionPrefix=token.slice(0,2), shortExplicitArg=token.slice(2); iterate the option strings in registration order and collect a match when opt === shortOptionPrefix (paired with shortExplicitArg) else when opt.startsWith(optionPrefix) (paired with null). Required consequences: '--h', '--he', '--hel' match only '--help'; '-hx' matches '-h' with explicit arg 'x'; '-a', '-abc', '-ap1', '---a', '--ab', '--A' match nothing.
- AMBIGUITY ERROR (in practice only reachable when the part before the first '=' is exactly '--', e.g. '--=x' or '--='): message is `ambiguous option: ${token} could match ${matches.join(', ')}` where token is the FULL original token including any '=value' and matches is the matching option strings in registration order - for this parser always '--help, --a, --b, --c, --d'. Exit 2.
- PHASE 2 - CONSUME, left to right, maintaining an `extras` array. On an UNKNOWN-OPTION token: push the raw token to extras and advance by one (do NOT swallow the following token). On a POSITIONAL or SEPARATOR token: since no positionals are declared, push the raw token to extras and advance by one. This index-by-index rule reproduces every observed extras list, including 'e1 e2 --z e3' and '-- --=x'.
- CONSUME a 0-argument OPTION (the help action): if explicitArg is null -> run the action now: print the help block to stdout and exit(0) immediately, skipping all further parsing and skipping the required-argument check. If explicitArg is non-null AND came from an '=' separator -> raise `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<explicitArg>'` and exit 2 (covers '--help=x', '--he=x', '-h=x', '--help=', '-h='; the empty string renders as ''). - CONSUME a 1-argument OPTION (--a/--b/--c/--d): if explicitArg is non-null the value is exactly that string (any content is legal: '', '-x', '--', 'x=y=z', spaces, newlines) and consumption advances by one token. Otherwise inspect the NEXT token's phase-1 classification: it must be POSITIONAL to be usable as the value. If there is no next token, or the next token is an OPTION, an UNKNOWN-OPTION, or the SEPARATOR '--', raise `argument ${optionString}: expected one argument` and exit 2. Classification, not raw text, decides: '-5', '-5.5', '-' and ' -x' are POSITIONAL and therefore valid values, whereas '-x', '--z', '--b=1', '--help' and '--' are rejected.
- LAST-WINS for repeated options: simply overwrite the stored value. '--a 1 --a 2' and '--a=1 --a 2' both store '2'.
- PHASE 3 - REQUIRED CHECK, after consuming and BEFORE reporting extras. If any of a,b,c,d were never set, raise `the following arguments are required: ${missing.join(', ')}` with missing in DECLARATION order --a, --b, --c, --d (never argv order) and exit 2. This must take precedence over unrecognized arguments: '--a p1 --z x' must print 'the following arguments are required: --b, --c, --d'.
- PHASE 4 - EXTRAS CHECK, only if nothing above errored. If extras is non-empty, raise `unrecognized arguments: ${extras.join(' ')}` and exit 2. Join with a single space, preserve argv order, echo tokens verbatim (an empty-string extra therefore leaves a trailing space in the message).

- NO positionals are declared, so any non-option token is always an extra. No fromfile support: a leading '@' has no special meaning. '+' is not a prefix character. Option matching is case-sensitive, so '--A' is not '--a'. The '--' separator must NOT be stripped - it appears verbatim in the unrecognized-arguments list.
